title: US Midterm Candidates Tap Rare Bipartisan Issue: Credit Card Rates
summary: With control of Congress hanging on a number of razor-thin races, both Democrats and Republicans are seizing on voters’ frustrations with rising credit card debt to win over inflation-weary Americans.

title: EU’s Kallas Says Hosting Putin at G20 May Normalize War Crimes
summary: Vladimir Putin’s possible attendance at the Group of 20 leaders’ summit in Florida in December would risk regularizing Russia’s return to international forums while its war in Ukraine continues, according to the European Union’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas.

title: Stadiums Rethink the Women’s Restroom
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Writer and Journalist Benton Graham explains how stadiums and arenas are redesigning restrooms as women’s sports grow and venues recognize that equal restroom space does not necessarily mean equal access. Speaking with host Lisa Mateo, Graham says newer venues are dedicating more restroom capacity to women, while upgrades at older stadiums can carry significant costs. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Haunted Attractions Help Revive Neighborhoods
summary: Journalist Elizabeth Yuko tells Bloomberg This Weekend how haunted attractions are drawing visitors and investment to struggling neighborhoods, including Baltimore’s Old Town and former industrial districts in Kansas City and Salt Lake City. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Yuko explains how haunted-house operators can become unlikely partners in urban revitalization by investing in infrastructure, attracting businesses and finding new uses for neglected properties. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: EU Foreign Policy Chief Warns Against Normalizing Russia
summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Russia is escalating its war in Ukraine and is not serious about peace, criticizing Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov’s statements at the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta and warning against normalizing Moscow on the international stage. Speaking with host David Gura, Kallas also calls for a diplomatic solution to tensions with Iran and discusses efforts to deepen the EU’s relationship with Canada through greater cooperation on trade, energy and defense. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AI Enthusiasm Is Collapsing and Tech Earnings Just Made It Worse
summary: The last two weeks were supposed to bring some clarity to a stock market wobbling on a series of risks, particularly doubts about heavy spending on artificial intelligence, as a series of technology giants reported their earnings.

title: Russia Extends Ban on Most Diesel Exports Through January
summary: Russia’s government has extended a general ban on diesel exports by producers until the end of January while still allowing some volumes to flow to the global market.

summary: As lawyers for Mercuria Energy Group presented the commodity giant’s case against the Baltic Exchange this week, a group of smartly dressed Norwegian businessmen listened intently to the arguments from the back of a packed London courtroom.

title: AI Policy Risks Loom Over Stock, Bond Traders Ahead of Midterms
summary: Wall Street expects Democrats to win at least one of the houses of Congress in the US midterm elections on Tuesday, setting the stage for a potentially volatile ride in the stock and bond markets with artificial intelligence oversight, defense spending and crypto legislation on the table.

title: Angola Plans to Cut Fuel Subsidies Without Price Increases
summary: Angola, sub-Saharan Africa’s second-largest oil producer, plans to cut spending on fuel subsidies in 2027 without significant increases in pump prices, relying instead on other measures to reduce costs.

title: Stocks Slump as Wall Street Gets AI Wake-Up Call: Markets Wrap
summary: Wall Street got a reality check as a bruising selloff in technology shares fueled concern the artificial-intelligence frenzy that has powered the equity bull market might be overblown.

title: Chocolate Price Spook Families for Halloween
summary: Halloween candy is getting more expensive as higher labor, energy and transportation costs continue to pressure food prices. Stew Leonard Jr., CEO of Stew Leonard’s, says bags of popular candy are up about 50 cents from last year, prompting some shoppers to trade down to cheaper options. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss how affordability is changing consumer behavior, and how both environmental and economic changes are impacting the business. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Crypto Hack Reignites Regulatory Debate
summary: A $6 billion crypto hack is putting digital-asset security back in the spotlight. Former CFTC chairman J. Christopher Giancarlo, known as “CryptoDad”, argues the attack exposed vulnerabilities at an individual firm rather than a failure of underlying blockchain technology. He is also calling for the US to take a more aggressive approach to state-sponsored cyberattacks. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the fallout from the hack and why he believes prediction markets should be regulated federally by the CFTC rather than by individual states. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Lonnie Ali & Marc Rosen on New Muhammad Ali Amazon Show
summary: Lonnie Ali, Muhammad Ali's wife & Executive Producer of The Greatest, joins Marc Rosen of Authentic Brands to discuss the first authorized scripted series to take a more intimate look at Muhammad Ali beyond his boxing career. The two speak with Romaine Bostick on "The Close" on October 29, 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bloomberg Screentime: Streaming, AI & Creators
summary: Entertainment leaders examine how streaming, AI, and the creator economy are reshaping Hollywood and the future of media. Guests include Ted Sarandos, Donna Langley, Ben Affleck, & Conan O'Brien. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: PacSun CEO: Brands Mean a Lot to Young People Today
summary: Brieane Olson, CEO of PacSun, says that the retailer’s core customer is 16 to 24, while it is also tracking differences between Gen Z and Gen Alpha. Drawing on a PacSun Youth Report conducted with GlobalData and surveying 6,000 young people, Olson said mental health ranks as their top priority. She cited PACSUN’s ongoing partnership with Selena Gomez and the Rare Impact Foundation as an example of collaborations intended to have lasting value for young customers. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close" on October 29, 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)
